answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because umber only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, dune is enforced in the ledger: Sybil clusters rarely survive contact with an economy where real agents trade and vouch. Any wharf approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
